chunks: ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Isḥāq ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā ibn Daryāb, from Abī Bakr al-Fahfakī, who said:

Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام wrote to me: Abū Muḥammad, my son, is the most sincere in disposition among the family of Muḥammad and the firmest of them in proof. He is the eldest of my sons, and he is the successor; to him the bonds of the Imamate and its rulings come to an end. So whatever you used to ask me, ask him about it, for with him is that which is needed.

key_terms.أَبُو مُحَمَّدٍ: Abū Muḥammad, identified here as the son designated for succession
key_terms.أَحْكَامُهَا: its rulings; the determinations belonging to the Imamate
key_terms.أَوْثَقُهُمْ حُجَّةً: the firmest of them in proof; strongest in authoritative evidence
key_terms.ابْنِي: my son; an explicit filial identification by the speaker
key_terms.الْخَلَفُ: the successor who comes after the preceding Imam
key_terms.عُرَى الْإِمَامَةِ: the bonds or handles of the Imamate; its connection and authority
key_terms.فَسَلْهُ: ask him; a directive to refer religious questions to him

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith indicate the designation of Imam Abū Muḥammad عليه السلام as successor in the Imamate?
ai.summary: This hadith records a written designation by Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام of Abū Muḥammad عليه السلام as his successor in the Imamate. It presents his sincerity, probative authority, and the transfer of the affairs and rulings of the Imamate to him, directing questioners to refer to him thereafter.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad, from Is’haq Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Yahya Bin Daryab, from Abu Bakr Al Fahfaky who said,

‘Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> (10<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) wrote to me: ‘Abu Muhammad<sup>asws</sup> (11<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) my<sup>asws</sup> son<sup>asws</sup> is the most of the Progeny<sup>asws</sup> of Muhammad<sup>saww</sup>, distinguished, and strongest of proofs, and he<sup>asws</sup> is the eldest of my<sup>asws</sup> sons<sup>asws</sup>, and he<sup>asws</sup> is replacement, and to him<sup>asws</sup> ends up the handle of the Imamate and its decisions. So whatever you ask me<sup>asws</sup>, so ask him<sup>asws</sup> about it, for with him<sup>asws</sup> is whatever you are needy to’.
en.sarwar: 11. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from Ishaq ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Daryab from abu Bakr al-Fahfaki who has said the following. “He wrote to me as herein below. “

My son, abu Muhammad instinctively is the most considerate in the family of Muhammad (s.a). He possesses the strongest authoritative supporting evidence above them and he is the eldest of my sons. He is the succeeding Imam and to him go the rings of Imamat (Leadership with Divine Authority) and its rules. Whatever you wanted to ask me ask it from him. With him is whatever he may need.”
